svg.title: Through a priestly grandfather
svg.text: Through a priestly grandfather
Rabba bar Avuh’s cases: ten certain firstborn donkeys, or smoothed untithed piles
1 · An Israelite
The donkeys were born in his domain, so they need redemption (Rashi);
the produce in his house owes teruma and tithes.
bequeathed to his daughter’s son
2 · A priest: the heir’s mother’s father
He would have designated lambs and kept them himself, since he is a priest
(Rashi); he could also separate the teruma and keep it.
bequeathed to his daughter’s son
3 · An Israelite heir
Donkeys:
designates ten lambs, tithes them, and they are his.
Produce:
separates teruma and tithes, and it is his.
As if the priest had separated them and left them to him.
Why both rulings are needed
Donkeys alone: perhaps only there, since the lamb “stands separated,” while unseparated gifts
are as if not separated. Produce alone: perhaps only there, since it is tithed from itself,
while for a donkey a lamb must be brought from elsewhere.
